analysis: The only change in this PR is a documentation addition to docs/developer/test.md (head lines 551-561). It adds a test command for LocalTokenizerByteFallbackTests. The new text describes a synthetic-tokenizer decode test: Gemma 4 byte-fallback `<0xHH>` tokens must survive whole decodes, streams, segment restarts and trailing special tokens, a run cut inside a character must end in one U+FFFD, and the unknown token must not decode as a byte. A literal `<0x41>` token on another decoder keeps its spelling. No source, workflow, protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization, encryption or cache code is modified. The text introduces no new attack surface and does not alter any control from the threat model (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, T-041 and others). The test command uses only a `--filter` argument and reads no secrets or network resources. I also read the surrounding unchanged test.md content in both units. It describes existing qualification and CI procedures, such as the App Attest provider dispatch tests, native serving qualification, release lanes, the SSD write-budget test and the cache epoch tests. None of those descriptions were changed by this PR. Remaining integration questions: the production LocalTokenizerLoader and decoder code is outside the supplied evidence, so this review says nothing about the correctness of the byte-fallback decoder itself. It is a documentation change only, so no deeper review is needed.
